With Election Day nine days away, the 2026 midterm campaign entered its closing weekend with both parties' biggest names on the trail. President Donald Trump cast an early ballot Saturday in West Palm Beach, Florida, telling reporters he voted the party line “very much so,” according to the Associated Press, then rallied supporters in Perry, Georgia, where he announced that Audi will build its first U.S. factory in Georgia — an investment Audi puts at about $4 billion and roughly 4,500 jobs.

Former President Barack Obama, meanwhile, held his first rallies of the midterm season Saturday, campaigning in Cleveland, Ohio, for Amy Acton and Sherrod Brown, and in Detroit, Michigan, for U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and gubernatorial candidate Jocelyn Benson. Reuters quoted Obama framing the November 3 vote as a “circuit breaker” to “at least rein in some of the foolishness” of Trump's presidency, and accusing Trump of corruption. The White House did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.

Trump's closing-weekend swing continues Sunday at 3 p.m. with a rally at McMorran Place Arena in Port Huron, Michigan, where lines were already forming early Sunday morning, according to the Port Huron Times Herald. Michigan's early in-person voting began Saturday and runs through Sunday, November 1. In the Michigan Senate race, El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers, a former U.S. representative, Reuters reported.

The stakes are control of a closely divided Congress, and the closing arguments are now being delivered in person, state by state. For Webb County readers, the parallel is close to home: early voting here runs through October 30, and Election Day is Tuesday, November 3 — the same ballot deadline driving the national sprint.

What to watch next: whether the closing-weekend rallies move early-voting numbers in battleground states, and how the final week of national messaging filters into down-ballot races in Texas and across the border region.

title: Midterms closing weekend: Trump votes early, Obama hits the trail for the first time
